messages:
cassie: Opening a focused docs PR to harmonize function/tool calling examples (all SDKs), add a small "robust parsing" recipe for streaming outputs, and do a link sweep. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5299 — looking for quick reviews and to triage any CI snags.

liam: I'm on Ruby + CLI examples. Will switch the old `invoke_tool` samples to the new API and add a tiny CLI example showing `redwood call-tool --name search --input '{"q":"x"}'`.

omar: I'll take Python and the general parsing advice. Suggest we show two patterns: 1) buffering SSE/chunked streams until a full JSON envelope; 2) a small repair fallback that trims leading/trailing garbage (useful when model spits HTML wrappers).

rachel: Quick note: I've seen LLM outputs wrapped in `<pre>` or extra markdown fences. I'll draft a tiny helper to strip common wrappers before JSON.parse/unmarshal. Example regex: `resp_text.sub(/^\s*<pre[^>]*>/i, '').sub(/<\/pre>\s*$/i, '')` (Ruby pseudo).

liam: Ruby draft for call_tool snippet:
```ruby
resp = client.call_tool(name: "search", input: { q: "weather" })
result = JSON.parse(resp.body)
```
Also adding a CLI example and a one-line note about large payloads and backpressure.

omar: Python buffering sketch:
```python
# buffer SSE/chunked stream, then parse once complete
buf = ''
for chunk in client.stream_tool(...):
    buf += chunk
obj = json.loads(strip_wrappers(buf))
```
And a fallback: try json.loads, on JSONDecodeError -> attempt simple repair (find first/last braces) then retry.

docs-bot: link-checker ran on branch -> 5 broken example links detected, comments added to PR.

ci-bot: docs-ci/snippet-lint failed on `examples/old_invoke_example.md` — linter flagged deprecated `invoke_tool` usage and malformed fenced code.

cassie: OK, plan: liam will patch Ruby/CLI and remove deprecated invoke samples, omar will add the buffering + repair recipes and the html-wrapper strip helper, rachel will add the Ruby wrapper example and a short guardrail paragraph recommending enums/discriminators for action routing. I'll push link fixes and re-run the link-check. Target: small follow-up PR for Private docs translations after merge. Any blockers?

liam: No blockers. I'll open a quick PR to fix the linter error and update CLI examples.

omar: No blockers. I'll include a tiny pytest that asserts repair path works for a streaming token-split case.

rachel: I'll add the wrapper-strip helper and a 1-line rationale for enums (deterministic routing, easier tests).

cassie: Thanks — tagging @liam @omar @rachel. I'll wait for the fixes and then re-run docs-ci. Hoping to merge by tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
